The '''2021–22 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Michigan]] during the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. This season marked the program's 106th season and its 105th consecutive year as a member of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. The Wolverines, led by third-year head coach [[Juwan Howard]], played their home games for the 55th consecutive year at the [[Crisler Center]] in [[Ann Arbor, Michigan]].

==Previous season==
The [[2020–21 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Wolverines]] finished the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21 season]] 23–5, 14–3 in [[2020–21 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to its first Big Ten regular season championship since [[2013–14 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2014]]. As the No. 1 seed in the [[2021 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they defeated [[2020–21 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team|Maryland]] in the quarterfinals before losing to [[2020–21 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]] in the semifinals. The Wolverines received an at-large bid to the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 1 seed in the East region, where they defeated [[2020–21 Texas Southern Tigers basketball team|Texas Southern]] and [[2020–21 LSU Tigers basketball team|LSU]] to advance to their fourth straight Sweet Sixteen. In the Sweet Sixteen, they defeated [[2020–21 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]] before being upset by No. 11-seeded [[2020–21 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|UCLA]] in the Elite Eight.

==Regular season==

===November===
Michigan began the season on November 10 with an 88–76 victory over the [[Buffalo Bulls men's basketball|Buffalo Bulls]], winning their 19th consecutive season opener. Michigan was led by [[Hunter Dickinson]] with 27 points, his sixth career game with 20 or more points, while Terrance Williams II added a career-high 15 points and seven rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401364997|title=Dickinson-led No. 6 Michigan beats Buffalo 88-76 in opener|access-date=November 10, 2021|date=November 10, 2021|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2021/11/10/mens-basketball-michigan-opens-season-with-victory-over-buffalo-behind-dickinsons-27-points.aspx|title=Michigan Opens Season with Victory Over Buffalo Behind Dickinson's 27 Points|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|access-date=November 10, 2021|date=November 10, 2021|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On November 13, Michigan defeated [[Prairie View A&M Panthers basketball|Prairie View A&M]] 77–49. Michigan was led by [[Eli Brooks]] with 15 points, while [[Caleb Houstan]] added 13 points, and Dickinson added 11 points, including his first career three-pointer, and 10 rebounds, for his seventh career double-double.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401372133|title=No. 6 Michigan rolls past Prairie View A&M 77-49|access-date=November 13, 2021|date=November 13, 2021|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2021/11/13/mens-basketball-michigan-runs-to-victory-over-prairie-view-a-amp-m-in-coaches-vs-racism-game.aspx|title=Michigan Runs to Victory over Prairie View A&M in Coaches vs. Racism Game|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|access-date=November 13, 2021|date=November 13, 2021|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On November 16, Michigan was upset by [[2021–22 Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball team|Seton Hall]] 67–65 in the [[Gavitt Tipoff Games]]. Michigan was led by Dickinson with a career-high 33 points, nine rebounds, and a career-high-tying four blocks, while Houstan added 16 points, and Williams recorded a career-high-tying three three-pointers off the bench.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401412488|title=Dickinson scores 33, Michigan beats Michigan St. 87-70|access-date=March 1, 2022|date=March 1, 2022|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2022/3/1/mens-basketball-michigan-rolls-past-michigan-state-behind-dickinsons-career-best-33-points.aspx|title=Michigan Rolls Past Michigan State Behind Dickinson's Career-Best 33 Points|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|access-date=March 1, 2022|date=March 1, 2022|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On March 3, Michigan lost to (No. 24 AP Poll/No. 25 Coaches Poll) Iowa 82–71. Michigan was led by Dickinson with 21 points, 11 rebounds and four blocks for his tenth double-double of the season, while Brooks added 17 points, Houstan added 11 points and Jones added 10 points and a team-high six assists.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401364472|title=No. 24 Iowa beats Michigan 82-71 for 5th straight victory|access-date=March 3, 2022|date=March 3, 2022|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2022/3/3/mens-basketball-michigan-drops-home-finale-to-no-24-iowa.aspx|title=Michigan Drops Home Finale to No. 24 Iowa|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|access-date=March 3, 2022|date=March 3, 2022|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On March 6, Michigan defeated (No. 23 AP Poll/No. 25 Coaches Poll) Ohio State 75–69. Michigan was led by Jones with 21 points, while Williams added 17 points off the bench, and Diabaté added seven rebounds and two assists.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401364478|title=Jones, Michigan beat No. 23 Ohio State; B10 tourney up next|access-date=March 6, 2022|date=March 6, 2022|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2022/3/6/mens-basketball-wolverines-rally-for-road-win-at-no-23-ohio-state-in-regular-season-finale.aspx|title=Wolverines Rally for Road Win at No. 23 Ohio State in Regular Season Finale|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|access-date=March 6, 2022|date=March 6, 2022|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref>

==Postseason==
===Big Ten tournament===
On March 10, Michigan opened its [[2022 Big Ten men's basketball tournament]] play with a 74–69 loss to Indiana in the second round. Michigan was led by Jones with 18 points, four rebounds, three assists and two steal, while Brooks added  17 points, four steals, three assists and two rebounds in his 100th career start, and Dickinson added 15 points and five rebounds. Jones surpassed 1,600 career points and 600 rebounds for his collegiate career.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2022/3/10/mens-basketball-wolverines-fall-to-hoosiers-in-big-ten-tournament-second-round.aspx|title=Wolverines Fall to Hoosiers in Big Ten tournament second round|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|access-date=March 10, 2022|date=March 10, 2022|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref>

===NCAA tournament===
On March 13, Michigan received an at-large bid to the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2022 NCAA tournament]] as the No. 11 seed in the South Region.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2022/3/13/mens-basketball-michigan-receives-ncaa-no-11-seed-will-face-colorado-state-in-indianapolis.aspx|title=Michigan Receives NCAA No. 11 Seed, Will Face Colorado State in Indianapolis|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|access-date=March 13, 2022|date=March 13, 2022|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On March 17, Michigan begain their participation in the 2022 NCAA tournament with a 75–63 victory over (No. 24 AP Poll) [[2021–22 Colorado State Rams men's basketball team|Colorado State]] in the first round. Michigan was led by Dickinson with a game-high 21 points, six rebounds and four blocks, while Brooks added 16 points, Collins added a career-high 14 points, and Houstan added 13 points. Michigan rallied and overcame a 15-point deficit in the first half, as Colorado State recorded eight consecutive three-pointers on nine Michigan turnovers. Michigan was without starting point guard Jones due to concussion protocol.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2022/3/17/mens-basketball-second-half-rally-delivers-first-round-upset-win-for-michigan-over-colorado-state.aspx|title=Second-Half Rally Delivers First-Round Upset Win for Michigan over Colorado State|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|access-date=March 17, 2022|date=March 17, 2022|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref>

On March 19, Michigan defeated (No. 5 AP Poll/No. 8 Coaches Poll) [[2021–22 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]] 76–68 in the second round to upset the No. 3 seed in the South Region. Michigan was led by Dickinson with 27 points, including 3-of-5 on three-point field goals, 11 rebounds, four assists, a block and a steal, while Brooks added 23 points, and five assists and Diabaté added 13 points and six rebounds. Dickinson and Brooks outscored the entire Tennessee roster in the second half, 33–31. With the win, the Wolverines advanced to the Sweet Sixteen for the fifth consecutive year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2022/3/19/mens-basketball-michigan-overpowers-tennessee-in-second-half-for-ncaa-second-round-upset.aspx|title=Michigan Overpowers Tennessee in Second Half for NCAA Second-Round Upset|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|access-date=March 19, 2022|date=March 19, 2022|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref>

On March 24, Michigan lost to (No. 6 AP Poll/No. 5 Coaches Poll) [[2021–22 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] 63–55 in the Sweet Sixteen. Michigan was led by Dickinson with 15 points, 15 rebounds, three assists and two blocks, for his second consecutive double-double of the tournament, while Brooks added 14 points, five rebounds, two assists and a steal. Michigan held Villanova to 9-of-30 on three-pointers, however, they struggled themselves, shooting just 21-of-61 from the field. After trailing by as many as nine points in the second half, Michigan reduced the lead to four points during the final 3:30 of the game. The Wolverines could not capitalize on three Villanova turnovers in the final 50 seconds of the game, as they made only one of their final 11 shots.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2022/3/24/mens-basketball-michigan-denied-return-trip-to-ncaa-elite-eight-by-no-2-seeded-villanova.aspx|title=Michigan Denied Return Trip to NCAA Elite Eight by No. 2-Seeded Villanova|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|access-date=March 24, 2022|date=March 24, 2022|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref>
